cases.prompt: Three requirement documents disagree about order cancellation. Synthesize the product decision and place durable artifacts in the existing repository docs hierarchy.
cases.expected_output: Uses $product-definition for source synthesis, recommendation, product decision authority, requirement and acceptance updates; uses $docs-governance only for documentation authority, artifact home, lifecycle, and router updates; neither owner absorbs the other.
expectations: Names the smallest lead and supporting knowledge owners plus their distinct bounded contributions.
Does not choose an execution workflow, create durable state, or turn a Router recommendation into project Authority.

cases.prompt: Accepted REQ-12, RULE-4, and AC-9 now need UI surfaces, interaction states, state owners, and proof needs.
cases.expected_output: Keeps user and product obligations with $product-definition, then has $interface-capability-planning reference those IDs and map them into surface, region, interaction-state ownership, and proof needs without redefining product rules or promoting layout choices into product semantics.
expectations: Names the smallest lead and supporting knowledge owners plus their distinct bounded contributions.
Does not choose an execution workflow, create durable state, or turn a Router recommendation into project Authority.

cases.prompt: Changing Order.status affects the backend writer, optimistic frontend state, realtime projection, and browser-visible recovery.
cases.expected_output: Uses $evolvable-application-architecture for fact authority, transaction and writer boundaries; $frontend-architecture for projection, Query/store/realtime reconciliation; and Harness/Test owners for bounded proof surfaces. Each reports its own not_proven boundary.
expectations: Names the smallest lead and supporting knowledge owners plus their distinct bounded contributions.
Does not choose an execution workflow, create durable state, or turn a Router recommendation into project Authority.

cases.prompt: The Preset recommends a naming rule that conflicts with an accepted project Standard and ADR.
cases.expected_output: Keeps project documentation authority and accepted tradeoff, treats the Preset as an unadopted candidate, records a keep-project or conflict disposition, and does not overwrite the project decision.
expectations: Names the smallest lead and supporting knowledge owners plus their distinct bounded contributions.
Does not choose an execution workflow, create durable state, or turn a Router recommendation into project Authority.

cases.prompt: A Harness Result passes one browser path in a local stack. A separately selected execution method wants to consume it and decide completion.
cases.expected_output: Carries source_ref, Proof Surface, dependency reality, claim_ceiling, observed, supports, not_proven, and evidence refs through a generic Evidence Envelope; the external execution owner decides completion and remains outside the core Router.
expectations: Uses a generic selected-execution boundary rather than a workflow-specific adapter.
Does not equate Harness pass with execution completion.
Does not promote execution state into product or documentation Authority.

cases.prompt: A new flow handles highly sensitive medical records, but this Suite has no dedicated security or privacy Skill.
cases.expected_output: Exposes the missing policy/security/privacy authority, limits architecture and product work to their owned decisions, requests the external accountable owner, and does not claim security, privacy, or legal design complete.
expectations: Names the smallest lead and supporting knowledge owners plus their distinct bounded contributions.
Does not choose an execution workflow, create durable state, or turn a Router recommendation into project Authority.

cases.prompt: Take over contradictory business material and an AI-generated MVP while acting as product and technical lead.
cases.expected_output: Selects only applicable rows from the source-takeover Owner Map: $product-definition separates source and accepted target; $docs-governance places authority and evidence; architecture Skills map current implementation structure; Effect is conditional on installed code; Harness/Test owners identify observed and unproven behavior. Source existence alone is not reported as reachable runtime behavior, and no fixed sequence is imposed.
expectations: Names the smallest lead and supporting knowledge owners plus their distinct bounded contributions.
Does not choose an execution workflow, create durable state, or turn a Router recommendation into project Authority.

cases.prompt: I started from a failing test and already know which product term and module are affected. Route the knowledge I need without forcing AGENTS, docs/README, planning, or a central recipe.
cases.expected_output: Selects the owning specialists and direct project Authority/Evidence surfaces from the current concern, treating repository entries and docs routers as optional edges rather than mandatory traversal nodes.
expectations: No ordered Route Procedure is emitted.
The failing test remains implementation evidence rather than accepted intent.
Only distinct decision owners are selected.

cases.prompt: Two accepted documents define different cancellation rules, but one applies to EU subscriptions in v3 and the other to US one-time orders in v2. Resolve the conflict.
cases.expected_output: Checks object, market, version, and product scope before choosing an owner; classifies the statements as scoped coexistence when both remain valid, and does not invent supersession or a central conflict record.
expectations: Uses Question-scoped Ownership and names the applicable Product/SSoT Homes for each scope.
Does not flatten legitimate variants into one rule or create a global conflict status machine.

cases.prompt: An accepted product decision changes a shared Order status and affects SSoT, an API enum, frontend projection, and evidence. One public compatibility choice is still undecidable. Continue everything else without prescribing a workflow.
cases.expected_output: Identifies the changed Product decision, affected SSoT/Contract/frontend/Evidence Homes, isolates the public compatibility decision with its accountable owner, and continues reversible unaffected updates while allowing owners to choose implementation order.
expectations: Creates an impact obligation through links, updates, explicit drift, or lowered claims rather than a propagation state machine.
Does not let one undecidable public-contract choice block unrelated work or let a binding constraint take over semantic ownership.

cases.prompt: Should this Rust capability port use a generic or dyn Trait? Product semantics and adapter selection time are already settled.
cases.expected_output: Routes directly to $evolvable-application-architecture's Rust projection and does not force $architecture-decision-system, product clarification, or a Suite workflow.
expectations: Selects the smallest semantic owner for an ordinary ecosystem decision.
Does not turn a local trait choice into durable ADIR or human escalation.

cases.prompt: The EAA map, frontend state ownership, Effect runtime composition, and current source disagree. Produce a scoped architecture health and diff.
cases.expected_output: Uses $architecture-decision-system as lead, composes bounded rules from $evolvable-application-architecture, $frontend-architecture, and $effect-best-practices, and retains source/evidence distinctions.
expectations: Uses owner-qualified claims and derived health findings.
Does not make the Architecture Decision System the semantic owner of every domain rule.

cases.prompt: Evaluate whether removing fixed output templates from $frontend-architecture improves a new Agent without semantic regression.
cases.expected_output: Routes to $skill-evaluation-system for baselines, corpus, ablation, failure attribution, hierarchical gates, and model-run evidence; frontend remains owner of its semantics.
expectations: Separates Skill behavior evaluation from frontend doctrine ownership.
Does not let a single judge score automatically change the canonical Skill.

cases.prompt: A new generation of coding model is available. Reassess and release the entire AI Coding OS Suite.
cases.expected_output: Routes explicitly to $ai-coding-os-evolution, uses $skill-evaluation-system and affected semantic owners, and treats the model release as a probe rather than automatic change authority.
expectations: Names capability profile, candidate, evaluation, release, and rollback boundaries.
Does not prescribe a fixed reviewer workflow or allow circular self-publication.

cases.prompt: Provider timeout behavior is unknown, while product semantics and architecture ownership are settled.
cases.expected_output: Routes the empirical question to the appropriate Harness/Test owner for a Probe Request, keeps architecture and product decisions settled, and carries does_not_decide/not_proven.
expectations: Routes Unknown by claim kind instead of to a central unknown manager.
Does not let an observation seize product or architecture authority.

claim_ceiling: Declared composition-eval structure and expected owner/claim boundaries only; no independent model-run quality, runtime installation, or production behavior claimed.
